body.stem: You need a single-purpose admin role for a junior IT staff member. The role's only responsibility is to manage Microsoft 365 product assignments for groups from the admin center. A compliance policy prohibits any built-in role that can modify user accounts or change group memberships. You need to assign a built-in Microsoft Entra role. Which role should you assign?

options.text: License Administrator
User Administrator
Groups Administrator
Helpdesk Administrator

explanation.correct: Per the documentation, you must be at least a Groups Administrator, License Administrator, or User Administrator to assign Microsoft 365 products to groups. License Administrator is the most narrow option and satisfies the compliance policy because it grants only product assignment permissions without the ability to modify user accounts or change group memberships.

perChoice.a: Correct: License Administrator is the most narrow built-in role that grants the ability to assign Microsoft 365 products to groups, and it does not include permissions to modify user accounts or change group memberships, which satisfies the compliance policy.
perChoice.b: User Administrator can manage all aspects of user accounts in addition to product assignments, which violates the compliance policy that prohibits any role that can modify user accounts.
perChoice.c: Groups Administrator can create, delete, and manage group memberships in addition to product assignments, which violates the compliance policy that prohibits any role that can change group memberships.
perChoice.d: Helpdesk Administrator is limited to tasks such as resetting passwords and managing sign-in for non-administrators; it does not grant the ability to assign Microsoft 365 products to groups.

body.stem: A user named Sara currently has Office 365 E3 via membership in the Sales-licensed-group. Sara is being transferred to a team that is provided access through the Engineering-licensed-group, which grants Office 365 E5. You need to migrate Sara between the two groups so that she does not experience a temporary loss of service access during the changeover. Which sequence of steps should you follow?

options.text: Add Sara to the Engineering-licensed-group, verify Sara has the new product activated on her account, then remove Sara from the Sales-licensed-group
Remove Sara from the Sales-licensed-group, then add Sara to the Engineering-licensed-group
Remove Sara from the Sales-licensed-group, wait 30 days, then add Sara to the Engineering-licensed-group
Add Sara to both the Sales-licensed-group and the Engineering-licensed-group at the same time and remove her from the Sales-licensed-group the next day

explanation.correct: Per the documentation, to move a user between licensed groups without service interruption, add the user to the destination group first, confirm the new product is applied on the user's account, then remove the user from the original group.

perChoice.a: Correct: Adding Sara to the destination group first lets group-based licensing start applying the new product, then removing her from the original group after confirming prevents a temporary unlicensed state during the migration.
perChoice.b: Removing Sara from the source group first leaves her unlicensed until group-based licensing finishes processing the new assignment, which can cause a temporary loss of service access.
perChoice.c: The 30-day period relates to retention of mailbox data after a product is removed, not a recommended wait step for migrating users between licensed groups.
perChoice.d: Adding Sara to both groups simultaneously is not a documented procedure, and deferring removal to the next day reintroduces ordering risk rather than eliminating it.

body.stem: You assign the Office 365 E5 product to the Region-EMEA Microsoft 365 group in the admin center. The group has user accounts and other groups as members. You need to identify which members will receive the Office 365 E5 product from the group assignment.

exhibit.text:
Setting                                       | Value
-----------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------
Group name                                     | Region-EMEA
Group type                                     | Microsoft 365
User accounts added directly as members        | 30
Other groups added as members                  | All-Employees (contains 200 user accounts)
Product assigned to Region-EMEA                | Office 365 E5

options.text: The 30 user account members of Region-EMEA
The 30 user account members of Region-EMEA and the 200 user account members of All-Employees
Every user account in the Microsoft Entra directory
Only the 200 user account members of All-Employees

explanation.correct: Per the documentation, group-based licensing doesn't currently support nested groups. If you assign a product to a group, only the direct user members of that group receive the product; user accounts inside a nested group are not assigned the product through that membership.

perChoice.a: Correct: Only the 30 user accounts that are directly added as members of Region-EMEA receive the Office 365 E5 product through that group assignment; nested group members are not processed.
perChoice.b: The 200 user accounts inside All-Employees are nested members, not first-level members of Region-EMEA, so they do not receive the Office 365 E5 product through that membership.
perChoice.c: Group-based licensing scopes the assignment to members of the assigned group, not every user account in the directory.
perChoice.d: The 200 user accounts are nested inside All-Employees and are not direct members of Region-EMEA, so they do not receive the Office 365 E5 product through Region-EMEA.

body.stem: The Project-X group has Office 365 E3 with the Skype for Business service plan enabled. Twelve of its members have Audio Conferencing attached separately. You need to delete the Project-X group. You need to determine what happens to the members who have Audio Conferencing separately attached after the group deletion. What occurs for those members?

exhibit.text:
Property                       | Value
------------------------------|----------------------------------------
Group                          | Project-X
Service plans enabled         | Skype for Business
Members with a separate thing | 12 members have Audio Conferencing separately

options.text: Their Office 365 E3 inherited from the group is changed into a standalone entry on their user profile
Both their Audio Conferencing standalone entry and the Office 365 E3 entry are immediately removed
The deletion fails and the group remains because of unresolved dependencies
Office 365 E3 service plans are removed and Audio Conferencing stops working for those members

explanation.correct: Per the documentation, when a licensed group is deleted and a member has a separate entry that depends on a service plan from the group, Microsoft Entra ID may convert the inherited entry into a direct assignment so the dependent service keeps working. Audio Conferencing depends on Skype for Business, so Office 365 E3 inherited from Project-X is converted into a standalone assignment.

perChoice.a: Correct: Audio Conferencing depends on Skype for Business, so the inherited Office 365 E3 is converted into a standalone assignment on the member's profile so the dependent service continues working after the group is deleted.
perChoice.b: The dependency between Audio Conferencing and Skype for Business means the inherited Office 365 E3 is converted to a standalone assignment rather than being removed alongside Audio Conferencing.
perChoice.c: The group can be deleted; the issue is post-deletion behavior on dependent entries, not a deletion failure.
perChoice.d: Audio Conferencing cannot keep working without Skype for Business; the conversion is specifically designed to keep the dependent service functional, so it does not stop working.

body.stem: Multiple Microsoft 365 groups in your tenant have product assignment errors. You need to identify every group with errors so each one can be opened and the affected members reviewed. You need to choose the admin center path that lists all groups with errors. Which path should you use?

exhibit.text:
Need                           | What it does
-------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------
Locate groups with errors      | A summary screen with an info box that lists groups with errors
Locate users with errors       | A per-product user listing that shows reasons for failure
Inspect a specific group       | A per-group screen that surfaces a notification if errors exist
See consumption figures        | A report that shows allocated versus assigned counts

options.text: Billing > Licenses > Overview
Billing > Licenses > [product] > Errors & issues
Groups > [group] > Notifications
Reports > Licensing usage

explanation.correct: Per the documentation, in the Microsoft Entra admin center, Billing > Licenses > Overview displays an information box if any groups have product assignment errors; selecting the box opens the full list of groups with errors that can be opened individually to review affected members.

perChoice.b: Billing > Licenses > [product] > Errors & issues shows the users who have errors for one specific product; it does not produce a tenant-wide list of groups with errors.
perChoice.c: Groups > [group] > Notifications only shows the notification present on a particular group's page; it does not enumerate every group with errors across the tenant.
perChoice.d: Reports > Licensing usage shows subscription usage metrics, not groups with product assignment errors.

body.stem: You assign the Office 365 E5 product to a security group named Field-Engineers by using the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK. The group has 50 direct user members and one group named Contractors that itself has 30 user members. After the command completes, 50 users have the license and 30 users do not. You need to identify the cause of the partial result.

options.text: The Office 365 E5 tenant has fewer than 80 seats available, so the assignment reached only a portion of the members.
Set-MgGroupLicense can only apply licenses to Microsoft 365 groups; switching the group type would resolve the issue.
Group-based licensing applies the assignment to first-level members of the target group; members of inner groups are skipped.
Group-based licensing requires the target group to contain no more than 50 direct members before any assignments are processed.

explanation.correct: Per the documentation, group-based licensing does not currently support groups that contain other groups. When a license is assigned to a group that has nested groups, only the direct (first-level) members receive the license; members of the inner groups are skipped. In the scenario, Field-Engineers contains Contractors, so its 50 direct users received Office 365 E5 while Contractors' 30 users were skipped.

perChoice.a: The tenant seat count is unrelated; the cmdlet returns a seat-count error and would not report 50 successful assignments if seats were exhausted.
perChoice.b: Both security groups and Microsoft 365 groups support group-based licensing; switching the group type would not change the nested-group behavior.
perChoice.d: There is no documented 50-direct-member cap that prevents processing before the count is reached; large groups are supported, with the documented performance caveat only for very large groups.

body.stem: A security group named Analysts has Office 365 E3 assigned and the active plans for that group include SharePoint. You attempt to add Microsoft Workplace Analytics to the Analysts group. The addition fails for every member with an error indicating a missing prerequisite. You need to identify the cause.

exhibit.text:
Group: Analysts (Security)
Products assigned: Office 365 E3
Active plans in the group: SharePoint, OneDrive for Business, Teams

Result of Workplace Analytics addition:
  Licensing failed for all 120 members
  Reason: PrerequisiteServicePlanRequired

options.text: Workplace Analytics is incompatible with Office 365 E3 and must instead be paired with a higher-tier license.
Workplace Analytics can only be assigned to a group whose membership is below a certain limit.
Workplace Analytics requires an Exchange Online plan to be activated in the group assignment, but no Exchange plan is selected.
Workplace Analytics can only be assigned through individual user license management; the service plan must be added directly to each user.

explanation.correct: The documentation lists Microsoft Workplace Analytics as an add-on that requires an Exchange Online plan (Exchange Online Plan 1 or Exchange Online Plan 2) as a prerequisite in the same group. Because the Analysts group's set of active plans contains no Exchange Online plan, the addition cannot succeed, and the prerequisite requirement is the cause.

perChoice.a: Workplace Analytics works alongside Office 365 E3 as long as a qualifying Exchange Online plan is present in the same group; an E5 license is not required.
perChoice.b: Add-on assignments are not gated by a documented per-group membership floor specific to Workplace Analytics.
perChoice.d: Add-ons such as Workplace Analytics can be assigned at the group level when their prerequisite is met in the same group, so per-user assignment is not the only option.

body.stem: A user named Priya is a member of the Sales-Licensed group, which has the Office 365 E3 product assigned at the group level. Priya did not receive the product even though the assignment was attempted. You confirm that Priya's usage location was missing on the user object. You have now set Priya's usage location to United States. You need to apply the license to Priya.

exhibit.text:
User: Priya Singh (priya@contoso.com)
Usage location: United States
Member of: Sales-Licensed
Direct license assignments: (none)
Inherited licenses from groups: Office 365 E3

options.text: Remove Priya from the Sales-Licensed group and add her back to trigger a fresh assignment run.
From the Errors & Issues tab on the product details page, select Priya and choose Reprocess.
Delete Priya's user account and recreate it with the corrected usage location so the assignment starts over.
Assign the Office 365 E3 product directly to Priya instead of waiting for group-based processing to apply the inherited license.

explanation.correct: After correcting the underlying user-level cause (missing usage location), the documented procedure is to open the product details, go to the Errors & Issues tab, select the affected user, and choose Reprocess. The cmdlet or the user membership removal-and-readd would requeue processing, but the documented admin-center flow uses the Reprocess action on the Errors & Issues tab for this exact case.

perChoice.a: Removing and re-adding the user does not force reprocessing for a corrected user-property issue; it can also cause a temporary loss of access for licensed services and is not the documented fix.
perChoice.c: Deleting and recreating the user account is destructive (data loss, sign-in reset, mailbox re-creation) and is not a documented remedy for a corrected usage-location issue.
perChoice.d: Assigning the product directly bypasses the inheritance but does not address the corrected usage-location cause and creates a parallel direct assignment; Reprocess is the recommended step.

body.stem: Your team is documenting group-based licensing concepts for new administrators. For each item, drag it into the slot that best describes the matching real-world purpose. Each item will be used at most once.

items.text: Inherited assignment
Direct assignment
Group-based licensing
Licenses page
Errors & issues tab

slots.label: License applied to a user through their group membership
License applied on the user record itself, not through a group
An admin approach that applies licenses to many users by configuring one collection at a time
The admin surface where you assign, view, and modify licenses for individual users and groups
Section on the product details page listing every user who failed to receive that license

explanation.correct: Each documented concept matches the real-world purpose described in the slot: an inherited assignment is how group members receive a license; a direct assignment is applied on the user object; group-based licensing is the approach of configuring one collection to license many users; the Licenses page is the central admin UI for license management; and the Errors & issues tab lists users for whom the license assignment failed.

perChoice.a: Slot s1: inherited assignment is the term for a license that comes to a user through their group membership.
perChoice.b: Slot s2: direct assignment is the term for a license applied directly to the user record, not via group membership.
perChoice.c: Slot s3: group-based licensing is the concept of applying licenses to many users by configuring a single collection.
perChoice.d: Slot s4: the Licenses page (Billing > Licenses) is the admin surface used to assign, view, and modify licenses for individual users and groups.
perChoice.e: Slot s5: the Errors & issues tab on a product page lists users for whom the license assignment failed.

body.stem: You are reviewing the documented behaviors of group-based licensing in Microsoft Entra ID. For each scenario in the slots, drag the outcome statement that best matches it into the slot. One item does not fit any of the listed scenarios.

items.text: The user might temporarily lose access to the licensed service during processing
The inherited license gets converted to a direct one so the dependent service keeps working
The licensing attempt fails because an add-on has no prerequisite service plan
Only direct (first-level) group users get the license; nested group users do not
The user's mailbox and proxyAddresses attribute get recalculated

slots.label: Remove Sara from one licensed group before she is added to the next licensed group
Delete a licensed group that grants Skype for Business to members who also have Audio Conferencing assigned directly
Try to assign a product that itself requires another base capability while the group lacks that base capability
Assign a product to an outer container whose members include other containers of users

explanation.correct: Each scenario triggers a documented group-based licensing behavior: removing a user from the source group before adding them to the destination group causes a temporary loss while processing; deleting a licensed group when members have directly assigned dependent services can convert the inherited license to direct so the dependent service keeps working; attempting to assign a product that requires a base capability while the group lacks that base capability causes the licensing attempt to fail; and assigning to a container whose members include other containers processes only the direct first-level users.

perChoice.a: Slot s1: removing the user from the source group first causes temporary service loss while the destination group's license is being processed.
perChoice.b: Slot s2: deleting a group while members have directly assigned dependent services converts the inherited license to a direct assignment so the dependent service keeps working.
perChoice.c: Slot s3: assigning a product that itself requires another base capability without that capability being present causes the licensing attempt to fail.
perChoice.d: Slot s4: when the direct recipients can themselves contain further users, only the direct first-level users receive the license; nested recipients do not.
perChoice.e: No slot: this item describes the separate Mail and proxyAddresses attribute change behavior, which is not represented by any of the listed scenarios.

body.stem: You need to recall the documented limits and behaviors of group-based licensing in the admin center. For each scenario in the slots, drag the appropriate limit or behavior statement that matches it into the slot. Each item is used at most once.

items.text: The admin center caps this at 20 groups per operation
The admin center caps this at 20 users per retry pass
The list is paginated and shows 999 users at a time
The user must be added to the destination group first to avoid service interruption
Only the direct (first-level) users receive the license; nested groups are not processed

slots.label: Bulk-apply a product to 25 different groups at one time from the admin center
Attempt again the licensing for 30 affected users at one time from the Errors & issues screen
Display the affected users whose licenses could not be applied
Move a user from one licensed group to another group with the same product
Assign to a security container that contains another container as a member

explanation.correct: Each scenario matches a documented group-based licensing limit or behavior from the admin center: bulk group assignment is capped at 20 groups per operation; reprocess retries are capped at 20 users per pass; the user list is paginated at 999 users at a time; moving users between licensed groups requires adding them to the destination group first to avoid service interruption; nested containers are not supported and only the direct first-level users receive the license.

perChoice.a: Slot s1: the admin center limits group license assignment to a maximum of 20 groups per operation.
perChoice.b: Slot s2: the admin center caps Reprocess attempts at 20 users per retry pass.
perChoice.c: Slot s3: the lists of users who were or were not successfully assigned are paginated and display 999 users at a time.
perChoice.d: Slot s4: moving a user between licensed groups requires adding the user to the destination group first to avoid service interruption.
perChoice.e: Slot s5: nested groups are not supported; only the direct first-level users receive the license while nested groups are not processed.

body.stem: You perform routine license administration from the Microsoft 365 admin center. For each task described in the slots, drag the documented UI element or button name that best matches the task into the slot. Each item will be used at most once.

items.text: Reprocess
Errors & issues
Assign licenses
Licenses and Apps

slots.label: Re-apply the license to a single user after their underlying issue was fixed
Show every user for whom the assigned product failed to apply
Make a chosen product available to every direct member of an existing collection at once
Open a pane on a single user profile where you select which offerings they can access

explanation.correct: Each scenario matches the documented admin center UI element or action: Reprocess retries applying the license to a single user after their underlying issue was fixed; the Errors & issues tab on a product page shows every user for whom the assignment failed; Assign licenses hands out a chosen product to every direct member of a collection; and the Licenses and Apps pane on a user profile is where you select which offerings they can access.

perChoice.a: Slot s1: Reprocess retries applying the license to the affected user or group after fixing the underlying issue.
perChoice.b: Slot s2: the Errors & issues tab on a product page lists all users who did not receive a license and the reason for the failure.
perChoice.c: Slot s3: Assign licenses on the Licenses page hands out a chosen product to every direct member of an existing collection at once.
perChoice.d: Slot s4: Licenses and Apps on the user profile is the pane where you select or deselect the included offerings for a single user.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft 365 tenant. A help-desk manager has asked you to provide staff training material on the immediate effects of removing a user's product license. For each workload in the slots, drag the outcome that matches it into the slot. One item will not be used.

items.text: Held for 30 days, then deleted and unrecoverable
Retained unless the user is deleted from the admin center or removed through directory synchronization
Compliance investigation tools can no longer return items from the mailbox
End users see Unlicensed Product and activation errors
Remain fully accessible with no change in experience

slots.label: Exchange Online mailbox data
OneDrive for Business files
eDiscovery search results
Microsoft 365 productivity apps

explanation.correct: The license-users-groups page documents what happens when a user's license is removed: Exchange Online mailbox data is held for 30 days and then deleted and unrecoverable; OneDrive for Business files are not deleted unless the user account itself is removed; the mailbox can no longer be located by compliance investigation tools such as eDiscovery or Content Search; and end users with installed Microsoft 365 productivity apps see Unlicensed Product and activation errors. No workload stays fully accessible because license removal always changes data access or app behavior.

perChoice.item-a: Matches Exchange Online mailbox data — the 30-day hold then permanent deletion is documented specifically for Exchange Online mailbox data after license removal.
perChoice.item-b: Matches OneDrive for Business files — these files remain unless the user account is deleted from the admin center or removed through directory sync.
perChoice.item-c: Matches eDiscovery search results — compliance investigation tools such as eDiscovery and Content Search can no longer return items from the mailbox once the license is gone.
perChoice.item-d: Matches Microsoft 365 productivity apps — installed apps display Unlicensed Product and activation errors when end users open them after the license is removed.
perChoice.item-e: No slot — every workload is affected in some way when a license is removed, so nothing remains fully accessible with no change in experience.

body.stem: You manage licensing for a tenant where products are sometimes placed on a person's own object and sometimes granted through group membership. One member of the Sales-Core group cannot receive what that group grants, and that product's Errors & Issues list reports a failure for this member. You need this member to end up with the group's product, including the mail service that comes with it.

rows: Placed on the person's own object

options.text: Remove the Office 365 E1 assignment held outside the group
Buy more Office 365 E1 licenses and assign them to the Sales-Core group
Add Exchange Online (Plan 1) to the Office 365 E3 granted to the Sales-Core group
Remove the Office 365 E3 from Sales-Core and give each member Office 365 E5 directly

explanation.correct: The person's account carries two Exchange Online plans at once: Exchange Online (Plan 1) from the Office 365 E1 on their own object and Exchange Online (Plan 2) from the Office 365 E3 that Sales-Core grants. These plans overlap, so the tenant refuses to apply the group's product. Clearing away the redundant Office 365 E1 removes the overlapping plan, after which the group's Office 365 E3 with Exchange Online (Plan 2) can be granted.

perChoice.fix:b: The failure comes from overlapping service plans, not from running short of licenses, so buying additional Office 365 E1 licenses leaves the conflict untouched.
perChoice.fix:c: Switching Exchange Online (Plan 1) on for Office 365 E3 puts both plans in the group's product as well, which adds to the overlap instead of clearing it.
perChoice.fix:d: Handing out Office 365 E5 directly leaves the person holding Office 365 E1 with its Exchange Online (Plan 1) at the same time, so both plans are still on the account and the same failure occurs.

body.stem: You are the License Administrator for a tenant. An employee on the marketing team bought a Microsoft 365 product with a personal credit card, and that subscription now shows up under your tenant's subscriptions. Two more employees still need access to the product.

rows: Bought by an employee with a personal credit card

body.statement: Before handing out the two remaining licenses, you should {{action}}.

options.text: Take over the purchase or trial subscription
Assign the licenses from the Licenses page
Cancel this subscription and order an identical one
Turn off recurring billing so it stops at the end of the term

explanation.correct: A subscription that an employee bought with their own credit card stays under that person's control, and an administrator cannot assign or unassign licenses for it. Taking the subscription over, or taking over a trial subscription, moves it under tenant control, after which licenses can be assigned normally.

perChoice.action:b: Assigning from the Licenses page only works for subscriptions the tenant controls; it does not change the ownership of this employee's subscription.
perChoice.action:c: Cancelling leaves the tenant without the existing subscription and its remaining licenses, and the documentation offers takeover rather than cancellation for this situation.
perChoice.action:d: Turning off recurring billing stops renewal at the end of the term, but it does not hand control of the current term's subscription to the tenant, so the licenses still cannot be assigned.

body.stem: You granted Office 365 E5 to the Sales-licensed group from the product's page in the Microsoft 365 admin center. The product's list shows a single row for the Sales-licensed group and no individual names. You need to know exactly which accounts are currently receiving the product through that group.

columns: Row in the Office 365 E5 assignment list

body.statement: To identify the individual accounts that receive the product through the group, you should open {{location}}.

options.text: Teams & groups > Active teams & groups and view the group's entries
The Office 365 E5 product page and expand the group row
Users > Active users and filter the list by Office 365 E5
The Errors & Issues tab of the Office 365 E5 product page

explanation.correct: When a product is granted to a group, the assignment list shows the group name in place of the individual accounts that inherit it. The individual recipients are listed as the entries of that group on the Active teams & groups page, which is where you go to see who actually receives the product.

perChoice.location:b: The product page shows only the group as a single row; it does not break that row down into the accounts inside the group.
perChoice.location:c: The Active users list shows accounts and their licenses but is not where the group roster itself is kept, so it can't answer who is inside the licensed group.
perChoice.location:d: The Errors & Issues tab lists only the accounts whose assignment failed, not everyone who inherited the product from the group.

body.stem: Your tenant owns two separate subscriptions and each one includes Microsoft 365 Business Premium. Leadership wants a single figure for how many of that product the tenant owns across both subscriptions. You need to report that figure from the Microsoft 365 admin center.
body.statement: The combined figure is reported on the {{page}}, which shows {{count}}.

options.text: Licenses page
Your products page
Active users page
Teams & groups page
13 licenses
5 licenses
8 licenses
two separate rows of 5 and 8

explanation.correct: Licenses for the same product are summed across every subscription the tenant holds, so the two subscriptions that hold 5 and 8 Business Premium units are reported there as one total of 13.

perChoice.count:b: This is only the amount in the first subscription.
perChoice.count:c: This is only the amount in the second subscription.
perChoice.count:d: Rows per subscription are how the other subscription list is laid out; this page replaces those rows with a single combined total.
perChoice.page:b: The Your products page lists one row for each subscription you own, even when several rows carry the same product, so it never produces a combined figure.
perChoice.page:c: The Active users page lists accounts and what each one has; it does not summarize owned units per product.
perChoice.page:d: The Teams & groups page lists groups and their entries, not owned units of a product.

body.stem: You grant a product that includes Exchange Online (Plan 2) to the Support-licensed group. Two members end up without it, and the product's Errors & Issues list reports that both accounts carry the same mail alias. You need both members to end up with the product.

options.text: Correct the duplicated value on the accounts, then reprocess the user or group assignment
Buy more licenses for that product, then reprocess the user or group assignment
Set the usage location on the two accounts, then reprocess the user or group assignment
Remove one of the two members from the group, then reprocess the user or group assignment

explanation.correct: Exchange Online licensing cannot be applied when two accounts hold the same proxy address. Once the repeated value is cleaned up on the affected account, reprocessing the user or the group applies the product again.

perChoice.fix:b: Adding units of the product does not remove the repeated mail alias, so the same two accounts would still fail.
perChoice.fix:c: A location only blocks a product when it is missing or set to a place where the service isn't offered; the reported problem here is the alias both accounts share.
perChoice.fix:d: Dropping one member removes that person from the group instead of solving the failure, and the alias is still repeated on the remaining account.

body.stem: Your Microsoft Entra tenant provides Office 365 products to users through group membership. A security group named FieldOps currently holds an Office 365 E3 product at the group level. On the product's Errors & Issues tab, you see 8 members in error and the subscription status shows 0 available units. Which action resolves the reported issue?
body.statement: To resolve the situation, you should {{slot1}}.

options.text: Buy more licenses, remove unused direct assignments, or free licenses from other sources
Disable a conflicting Exchange Online plan on the affected members
Set the usage location on the affected members and remove users in unsupported locations from the group
Add the prerequisite and the add-on to the same group

explanation.correct: The Errors & Issues information shows that the subscription has 0 available units, which corresponds to the documented 'Not enough licenses' error for group-based product assignment. The documented fixes for this error are to buy more licenses, remove unused direct assignments, or free licenses from other sources.

perChoice.slot1:b: Disabling a conflicting Exchange Online plan addresses the 'Conflicting service plans' error, not an exhausted subscription with no available units.
perChoice.slot1:c: Setting the usage location on each affected member and removing users in unsupported regions addresses the 'Usage location isn't allowed' error, not a subscription that has run out of units.
perChoice.slot1:d: Adding the prerequisite service plan alongside the add-on in the same group addresses the 'Products with prerequisites or add-ons' error, not a subscription that has run out of units.

body.stem: You administer licenses in a Microsoft Entra tenant that uses group-based licensing. You are troubleshooting assignment failures and need to match each observed scenario to the documented relationship that explains it. For each scenario in the slots, drag the documented product relationship that applies into the slot. Each item will be used at most once.

items.text: Requires Exchange Online Plan 1 or Exchange Online Plan 2 as a prerequisite
Depends on Skype for Business being present
Conflicts with Exchange Online Plan 1 because both cannot be active simultaneously
Converts to a direct assignment if the licensed group is removed while a dependent direct license exists

slots.label: An add-on product is the only assignment in a group, and no group member ends up with the add-on enabled
A communications add-on is assigned to a user whose other license grants Exchange Online but does not include the supporting communications service
Two different versions of Exchange Online apply to the same user through different paths, and the admin port lists this user as a license error

explanation.correct: Each slot scenario maps to a documented relationship. Slot s1 (an add-on assigned alone to a group with no members receiving it) corresponds to item a: add-ons such as Microsoft Workplace Analytics require Exchange Online Plan 1 or Plan 2 as a prerequisite, so assigning the add-on alone causes the assignment to fail. Slot s2 (a communications add-on failing because the supporting service is absent) corresponds to item b: Audio Conferencing depends on Skype for Business being present on the user. Slot s3 (two different Exchange Online versions on the same user through different paths producing a license error) corresponds to item c: Exchange Online Plan 1 and Exchange Online Plan 2 cannot be active for the same user at the same time, so the conflicting plans produce the documented error.

perChoice.a: Maps to slot s1. An add-on assigned alone to a group fails because the documented add-on relationship requires Exchange Online Plan 1 or Plan 2 as a prerequisite.
